observation.visible_scene: A still, fixed-camera view of a shallow puddle on asphalt beside a concrete curb with sparse grass. The water mirrors a pale sky and dark building shapes. Two localized sets of circular surface ripples are present over the excerpt; the curb, grass, puddle outline and reflections stay in place throughout, indicating no camera motion.
visible_changes: At t=0.000 an already-in-progress set of concentric ripples occupies the center-left of the puddle; from t=0.000 to about t=1.120 these rings grow outward (expansion, not translation) and their amplitude fades until they are barely visible.
Around t=1.200 a small splash crown / bulge appears at the right side of the puddle near the curb edge; over t=1.200–1.280 this protrusion collapses back into the surface.

From about t=1.600 onward a second, distinct set of concentric ripples forms centered near that right-side point and steadily expands outward through the end of the clip (t=3.200), with the ring spacing widening as the pattern grows.
The first ripple pattern and the second ripple pattern are separate events at different centers; the second begins while the first is already dissipating, not as a continuation of it.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause and onset of the first ripples (already underway at the crop boundary) are not shown.
The cause of the second splash (e.g. an incoming droplet or object) is not visible; only its surface effect is seen.
Whether the second ripple set fully dissipates after t=3.200 is unknown.
uncertain_details: Exact center positions of each ripple set are approximate due to the distorted reflection.
Whether the first ripples vanish completely before the second dominate is borderline in mid-clip frames.
The white/dark shapes on the water are reflections, not separate objects, and should not be tracked as moving entities.
